content: [{"id": "h_title", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Automations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_intro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Automation in tatva_connect is one engine, one shape — a Flow. A Flow is Trigger · When · Then: a trigger is an event on a record, the When is the criteria that must hold, and the Then is an ordered set of actions. A rule is a Flow that runs once; a journey is a Flow that waits and resumes. The sections below are configured in order — each one builds on the one before it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_enable", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turn it on. Everything ships dormant. Open Engine Switches and enable Workflow::Engine::run, tick Enabled on each Flow that should be live, and make sure the Field Allowlist names every field a Flow reads or writes \u2014 until then, nothing fires.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h_setup", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Field Allowlist. The fields a Flow may read and write are declared here first, per grain. A Flow can only test a field that is readable and only set a field that is settable, so this list is both the safety fence and the vocabulary every later step draws from — nothing a Flow does can reach a field it does not admit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Action Groups. A reusable bundle of effect actions is assembled here — for example update a field on the lead, then create the next task. A group is named once and then referenced by any Flow’s step, so the same effect is built and corrected in one place. Only the verbs the allowlist supports can be added.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Flows. The Flow is composed here as Trigger · When · Then: the trigger doctype and event are chosen, the When criteria are added from the allowlisted fields, and the Then is arranged as an ordered graph of steps that run the Action Groups above. A guard action (Require Fields / Require Location) is enforced at save time and can block the save; every other action runs after. Adding a Wait or a Branch turns the Flow into a journey that parks and resumes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h_ref", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Reference", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_ref", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Webhook Endpoints. A Flow that calls an external system does so through a curated native Webhook — its URL, headers and secret are configured once here, and a Flow picks it by name, so no Flow ever holds a raw URL or a credential. Every configured endpoint an operator has set is listed here as the in-place reference; Webhook Log records each delivery.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h_mon", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Monitor", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_mon", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Running Instances shows every journey in flight — which lead it belongs to, the node it rests at, and whether it is running, parked, done or failed. Signal Inbox holds the external events (an API result, a review completion) waiting to resume a parked Flow. Execution Log is one row per node executed — the audit trail of what each Flow did.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sp1", "type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}}, {"id": "c_setup", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Setup", "col": 6}}, {"id": "c_ref", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Reference", "col": 6}}, {"id": "c_mon", "type": "card", "data": {"card_name": "Monitor", "col": 6}}]
